nodes.label: Member
nodes.summary: Presses play, receives a rank-ordered list of OCA URLs and streams from the top-ranked one. Content is optimised dynamically per device and network conditions.

nodes.label: Playback Apps (AWS)
nodes.summary: Check user authorisation and licensing, then determine which specific files the playback needs for this client and its network conditions.

nodes.label: Steering Service (AWS)
nodes.summary: Picks OCAs using what they reported plus client info such as geolocation, generates URLs, and returns them rank-ordered. Logs the steering manifest to Kafka.
nodes.details: Proximity rank is by network proximity alone, from BGP-advertised IP ranges: the OCA site advertising the longest, most specific matching prefix is first.

nodes.label: Cache Control Service (AWS)
nodes.summary: Stores what OCAs report: health and capacity, BGP routes learned, files on disk. Also drives nightly fill and content placement.
nodes.details: The control plane services control fill behaviour (adding new files nightly), compute file storage/hashing and handle playback telemetry.

nodes.label: OCA inside an ISP
nodes.summary: Purpose-built cache appliance, provided free to qualifying ISPs. Stores encoded video/image files and serves HTTP/HTTPS. Holds no client data. ISPs control which customers are routed to it.
nodes.details: Storage servers: mostly HDD, 200 TB+, ~40 Gbps. Flash servers: SSD, up to ~100 Gbps, up to 18 TB (2017 post).

nodes.label: OCA at an IXP
nodes.summary: Same appliances installed at internet exchange points and interconnected with ISPs through settlement-free peering.

nodes.label: Nightly fill (off-peak)
nodes.summary: Popular content is pre-positioned during configurable off-peak windows. Placement uses consistent hashing with 1000 slices per server, extended by Heterogeneous Cluster Allocation for mixed hardware. OCAs can fetch from each other.

nodes.label: Steering + OCA logs (Kafka)
nodes.summary: Steering manifests and OCA server logs are joined to compute cache misses (content miss, health miss), measured from the client's view.

nodes.label: Control plane (AWS)
nodes.summary: Playback Apps, the Steering Service and the Cache Control Service, running in AWS.
nodes.details: Grouping container: it names the units the sources describe together. The components inside it are listed in the Components view.

nodes.label: Open Connect CDN
nodes.summary: Netflix's CDN: appliances in ISPs and IXPs plus the nightly fill process.
nodes.details: Grouping container: it names the units the sources describe together. The components inside it are listed in the Components view.

steps.caption: The client asks the Playback Apps service in AWS to play a title.
Playback Apps check authorisation and licensing, decide which files this device needs, and ask the Steering Service to pick OCAs.
The Steering Service uses the data OCAs have reported to the Cache Control Service: health, BGP routes and files stored.
It returns a rank-ordered list of OCA URLs, ranked by network proximity first, with unhealthy or content-less sites filtered.
The client connects to the top-ranked OCA and streams video from it. AWS never touches the video bytes.
OCAs continually report which files they hold, their health and the BGP routes they have learned.
The control plane decides what each cluster should hold, using predicted popularity and consistent hashing, accounting for mixed hardware.
Files are added during off-peak windows when bandwidth is cheap. OCAs can also pull from each other.
The steering manifest, including the proximity rank and filters applied, is logged.
OCAs log which files were actually streamed and how many bytes.
Joined per playback, a stream from a site below the first proximity rank counts as a cache miss: a content miss if files were absent, a health miss if the local site was saturated.
